title: Priming & Latency Sample Capture — week 2027-01-10
body:
Priming & Latency Sample Capture — Fleet update (notes from 2027-01-12 standup and follow-ups)

Summary:
- Goal this week: run a controlled priming/pre-warm experiment across three regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west) to measure end-to-end latency improvement for long-context (seq=1024) workloads and quantify marginal cost of prewarming.
- Focus areas: priming strategy (cold vs. warm pods), eviction behaviors (KV cache churn), sampling accuracy for p95/p99, and impact on dedicated vs. burst capacity.
- Experiment lead: Ethan. Data collection + sample extraction: Marisol. Ops changes and rollout gating: Asha.

Experimental setup (short):
- Time window: Jan 08 00:00 — Jan 11 23:59 (48h effective sampling after warm-up).
- Regions tested: us-west (NVIDIA A800 pool, 912 GPUs), us-east (A800 + mixed A100 fallback pool, 816 GPUs), eu-west (A800, 384 GPUs).
- Traffic profile: synthetic Poisson mix mirroring app-prod: 60% chat (avg len 128 tokens), 30% generation (avg 512), 10% long-context regen (1024).
- Two cohorts: baseline (no priming, standard autoscale) vs primed (5-minute prefix prewarm + KV cache seeding).
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency (token-first and total), cold-start rate, KV cache hit ratio, additional GPU-minutes consumed, observed cost delta (relative to baseline).

Key metrics (aggregated):
- Global fleet size used for test: 2,112 GPUs (sum of test pools across regions; note: we pulled out some dedicated capacity for the experiment).
- p50 (seq=1024) baseline: 240 ms/token. Primed: 180 ms/token (25% reduction).
- p95 (seq=1024) baseline: 1,020 ms/token. Primed: 720 ms/token (29% reduction).
- p99 (seq=1024) baseline: 2,900 ms/token. Primed: 2,250 ms/token (22% reduction).
- Cold-start rate (requests that hit a cold runtime path): baseline 7.8% -> primed 1.4%.
- KV cache hit ratio for long-context flows: baseline 62% -> primed 81%.
- Additional GPU consumption (priming overhead): +3.6% GPU-minutes during active priming windows.
- Cost change (direct infra cost modeled): +~3.1% during the experiment window; extrapolated to steady policy: ~+1.0% on average if priming only during predicted surge windows.

Observations and nuance:
1) Latency wins are largest for tail (p95/p99) and for models with sizable KV cache usage. For short-chat flows the improvement is smaller (p95 down ~12%).
2) Prewarming is most effective when paired with KV cache seeding from recent prefixes — simple runtime pre-spin without cache seeding gives only ~10-12% tail improvement.
3) us-east shows smaller relative gains vs us-west because of higher baseline autoscale priming (we already keep slightly warmer pools in us-east due to enterprise SLAs). eu-west sees the largest relative gain because cold churn was high during the test window.
4) Preemption-sensitive instances (spot/preemptible) complicate priming: when a primed node is reclaimed, the effective cold rate spikes briefly; mitigation requires quicker priming or reserving a small protected band.
5) The cost-to-tail tradeoff looks attractive for customer tiers that are latency-sensitive (enterprise/dedicated). For best-effort/low-cost tiers: leave unprimed or use selective priming (by route/model).

Incident notes (during experiment):
- Jan 09 03:42 UTC: brief ripple in us-west when a maintenance eviction policy kicked 48 spot nodes and our priming job overlapped the eviction window; observed transient p99 spike to 4.8s. Ticket: INFRA-4321 (follow-up: adjust priming schedule and coordinate with cloud maintenance windows).
- Jan 10 17:20 UTC: sample ingestion pipeline missed ~30 minutes of traces due to an index rotation bug in the sample-collector; patch PR #789 fixed it and backfilled missing spans.

Decisions (proposed):
- Adopt a two-mode priming policy: 1) route-level priming for premium routes/models (can enable persistent warm fraction up to 6% of region pool), 2) predictive surge priming triggered by short-term traffic forecasts for standard routes. This is a middle ground between cost and SLOs.
- Reserve a small non-preemptible "buffer band" in each region (target 1.5% of active GPUs) to hold primed pods that cannot be reclaimed mid-surge. This mirrors earlier proposals but with a smaller footprint.
- Implement KV-cache seeding for priming runs (copy small prefix sets used by top-10 heavy hitters) — this has outsized effect on tail latency.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Ethan: iterate priming scheduler to avoid provider maintenance windows and add retry/backoff on eviction (INFRA-4334). ETA: 2027-01-20.
- Marisol: finalize sample-extraction script and publish canonical p95/p99 histograms for each model family (sheet:1a2B3cPrimingSamples). ETA: 2027-01-15.
- Diego: prototype protected buffer band: terraform change + smoke test in eu-west. Create PR and performance benchmark. ETA: 2027-01-18.
- Asha: draft rollout policy doc for route-level priming (includes cost allocation, per-customer gradation, and safety gates). Share with product-hosted-api and sales for feedback. ETA: 2027-01-21.
- SRE/Monitoring (assign to oncall): add a "priming-loss" alert when primed pool loss >3% within 10m and p95 latency increases >25% vs baseline. Follow-up: refine alert thresholds after one production week.

Risks & open questions:
- Long term cost: the steady-state cost delta depends heavily on how much of the fleet we keep persistently warm and if model families change (new larger models increase per-GPU warm cost). Need fine-grained cost model.
- Preemption variance: in markets with aggressive spot reclaim behavior (some APAC clouds) priming may be less effective. We need region-by-region policy knobs.
- Measurement fidelity: current sample window is small—need multi-week sampling + traffic spikes to be confident about p99 behavior under real traffic patterns.

Notes for product & sales sync:
- If we move forward with route-level priming as a premium feature, we should draft pricing language that ties p95 guarantees to a priming budget (e.g., 3% reserved warm pool for X customers). Product suggestions welcome.
- Sales ask: quick one-pager describing expected latency improvement for enterprise customers (we can use p95 numbers above as a starting point).

Next steps / schedule:
- Jan 13–15: run extended three-week priming A/B for 2 customer-simulated traffic windows; expand to ap-south small pilot.
- Jan 18–21: collate multi-week metrics, finalize rollout doc, and schedule stakeholder review (product-hosted-api, eng-serving-runtime, srep).
- Jan 22: decision meeting: do we ship selective priming behind a feature flag for dedicated customers?

Appendix (quick raw snippets):
- Sample JQL for traces: service=runtime AND tag:model_family:llama2* AND trace.duration>500ms
- Top-heavy routes during window: /v1/generate-chat (42%), /v1/chat-stream (26%), /v1/long-context (8%)
- Raw cost note: priming overhead measured primarily as GPU-minutes — scheduling overhead small relative to compute time for large models.

If anything looks off in the numbers or you want a deeper breakdown by model-family or dedicated vs shared pools, flag in #infra-priming and I will drop the CSV of per-model histograms.

-- Asha
